chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn Muhammad said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him): 'What should I do if I intend to perform Tamattu'?' He said: 'Enter into ihram for Hajj and intend the Tamattu'. When you enter Mecca, perform Tawaf around the House, pray two rak'ahs behind the Maqam, perform Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then shorten (your prayers) and thus annul the Umrah and make it Tamattu'. It is permissible for him to not mention anything at all and simply intend the Tamattu'. This was narrated.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (one of the hills for Sa'i)
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةَ: Al-Mut'ah (Tamattu' - a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: How does a pilgrim perform the rituals of Hajj al-Tamattu' according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural flexibility in Hajj al-Tamattu', emphasizing that the pilgrim's intention (niyyah) at the start of ihram is sufficient, even if specific rites are not verbally recited. It highlights the Shia view that the Umrah component is completed through Tawaf, Salat, Sa'i, and Qasr al-Hajj, effectively 'breaking' the initial ihram state before the subsequent Hajj ihram. This underscores the practical ease granted to pilgrims, allowing them to focus on the spiritual intent rather than rigid verbal formulas.
